problem:
Find the radius of convergence $R$ of the series

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{x}^{n}}{{2}^{n-1}(n-1)!}=x+\frac{{x}^{2}}{2\cdot 1}+\frac{{x}^{3}}{{2}^{2}\cdot 2!}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{{2}^{3}\cdot 3!}+⋯\,.
$$
worked_solution:
To apply the ratio test, we define ${a}_{n}=\frac{{x}^{n}}{{2}^{n-1}(n-1)!}.$ Then, we calculate the ratio of two successive terms and take the limit as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{x}^{n+1}}{{2}^{n}n!}\cdot \frac{{2}^{n-1}(n-1)!}{{x}^{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{x(n-1)!}{2n!}| \\  & =\frac{|x|}{2}\cdot {lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(n-1)!}{(n-1)!n} \\  & =\frac{|x|}{2}\cdot {lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{1}{n} \\  & =\frac{|x|}{2}\cdot 0 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The series converges if $L<1.$ In this case, the convergence condition is satisfied for all $-\infty <x<\infty .$ Therefore, we conclude that the radius of convergence is $R=\infty .$
